6.  Costs incurred and allocated by ServCo 
 
Cost Allocation Manual and Service Agreements 
Costs incurred by ServCo and by other NGUSA subsidiaries in providing services to NGUSA client 
companies (Client Companies), including the Company, are set forth in the service agreements and its Cost 
Allocation Manual (Revised April 2017)  (CAM) and include, but are not limited to, labor and related 
overhead costs (e.g., salaries of officers and other employees, employee welfare expenses such as social 
security taxes, life insurance, pensions, post-retirement benefits other than pension, medical, dental and other 
welfare expenses), training costs, facilities costs, information technology costs, and costs related to vendor 
and other contract services.  The organization, conduct of business and method of cost allocation are designed 
to result in the performance of services and the provision of goods economically and efficiently for the benefit 
of the Client Companies at cost, fairly and equitably allocated among such companies. 
 
The purpose of the CAM is to serve as a guide as to the manner in which costs should be charged to the Client 
Companies by the company incurring the cost.  The prevailing premise of these cost allocation guidelines is 
that allocation methods should not result in subsidization of non-regulated services or products by regulated 
entities or subsidization of services or products from one regulated entity to another. 
 
The provision of administrative services to the Client Companies by ServCo is specified in service agreements 
filed with the respective utility regulatory commissions. 
 
Principles of cost allocation 
The following principles guide the allocation of costs of products or services provided by Servco and other 
operating subsidiaries to the Client Companies. 
 
 Direct charging or direct assignment is the preferred allocation methodology and is used if the cost of 
providing a product or service can be identified with the Client Companies receiving the benefit of that 
product or service.  Direct charging should only be used if the cost of providing a product or service to an 
individual Client Company can be isolated and reported separately from costs to provide other products or 
services and from costs to provide the same product and service to other Client Companies. 
 
 The costs of products and services that cannot be direct charged should be allocated based on cost 
  causative allocation bases representative of the underlying cost drivers of that product or service. 
 
 The cost allocation methodology should be comprehensive, transparent, stable and administratively 
manageable and cost effective. 
 The calculation of the cost allocation bases should be supported by a clearly defined methodology, model 
Exhibit______(RRP-2)
Schedule 2
Page 50 of 100


--- Page 216 ---
 
and supporting policy and procedure documentation. 
 
 The cost allocation methodology should accommodate changes in the size of the allocation bases from 
period to period based on changes in the underlying cost drivers; the allocation bases should not vary 
significantly from period to period for uncontrollable factors not related to the underlying cost drivers. 
 
 
 The calculation of the allocation bases should be updated at least annually and more frequently if needed 
to reflect significant events (e.g., the sale of a significant affiliate). 
 
Costs are defined among the following four categories for purposes of allocating the costs of products and 
services to the Client Companies. This hierarchy represents the order of methodologies used when allocating 
costs. These four cost categories are: 
 Directly Assignable – Expenses incurred for activities and services exclusively for the benefit of a Client 
Company. 
 
 Directly Attributable – Expenses incurred for activities and services that benefit more than one Client 
Company and which can be allocated based on direct measures of cost causation; for example, number of 
employees or number of customers. 
 
 Indirectly Attributable – Expenses incurred as a “cost of doing business” that do not relate to the provision 
of specific products and services.  The costs typically benefit all entities within the corporate umbrella. 
Examples include governance costs, Corporate Secretary costs, and investor relations costs.  These costs 
are typically allocated based on a general measure of cost causation, commonly referred to as the general 
allocator. Costs that cannot be directly identified with the provision of a particular product or service.  
This includes but is not limited to governance costs, insurance, and taxes as well the cost of services 
supporting ServCo such as ServCo accounting and recruiting for ServCo positions. The general allocator 
is the ratio of net plant, net margins and net operations and maintenance expenses, equally weighted. 
 
 Unattributable – Expenses incurred for activities or services that have been determined as not 
appropriate for apportionment to the Client Companies.  These costs relate primarily to activities such as 
corporate diversification, political or philanthropic endeavors and, as such, are charged directly to the 
parent company, NGUSA. 
 
To apply these principles, ServCo and the Client Companies accumulate costs in system orders.  The order 
design acts as the primary cost control element from which costs are billed to affiliates.  For each order, an 
order design documents a description of the order’s use and purpose, the activities associated with that 
particular order, and justification for the allocation methodology to be used for allocating the costs 
accumulated in the order.  Only one allocation methodology can be used for each order. 
 
Subsidiaries charge no more than actual costs for services provided to the Company and other regulated 
affiliates.  
 
The monthly settlements process includes only the costs accumulated in the open orders.  There is no markup 
or profit included in allocations to the regulated affiliates.  The allocations are based on the methodologies 
designated and described above.  Accordingly, the unit cost (price) charged to these affiliates, including the 
Company, is intended to reasonably approximate the actual costs of providing such services. 
 
Section 7 of the CAM lists those services provided by ServCo and the Client Companies to whom these services 
are provided.  These services are provided in accordance with the service agreements filed with the respective 
utility regulatory commissions.

Supplementary information to the Summary of Costs- KEDNY 
 
The total amounts recorded by the Company for the twelve-month period ended December 31, 2018 in general ledger accounts representing 
operating expenses are summarized in the table below.  The total ledger cost data (A) is the total of transactions recorded in the Company’s 
general ledger that relate to operating costs considered for recovery in customer rates. 
We have then subtracted items in the second column (B) costs incurred for energy efficiency programs and fleet, and accounting entries 
related to the accrual or deferral of regulatory accounting mechanisms, leaving the third column to show costs that the Finance Team selected 
and included in its examination (refer to the Notes to the Summary of Costs for more details on the method of selection).  Column C, and 
the immediately preceding columns (d-h), include amounts cross-referenced to the Summary of Costs.

Notes to the Summary of Costs- Service Company 
 
1. Background 
 
National Grid USA Service Company (“Service Company”) provides management, administrative, accounting, 
legal, engineering and other services to NG USA subsidiaries.  
 
Service Company is a wholly-owned subsidiary of National Grid USA (“NGUSA”).  NGUSA is a public utility 
holding company with regulated subsidiaries engaged in the generation of electricity and the transmission, 
distribution, and sale of both natural gas and electricity. NGUSA is a direct wholly-owned subsidiary of National 
Grid North America Inc. (NGNA) and an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary of National Grid plc, a public limited 
company incorporated under the laws of England and Wales. 
 
Service Company separately issues financial statements prepared in accordance with the accounting 
requirements of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) as set forth in its applicable Uniform 
System of Accounts and published accounting releases (together, the FERC USoA), as well as financial 
statements prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States 
(GAAP).  The subject matter presented in the Summary of Costs is prepared consistent with the “Basis of 
Accounting” described in notes below, which are not necessarily the same as the accounting requirements of 
the FERC USoA or GAAP. 
 
2. Vendor Costs 
 
Summary of Selected Vendor Costs – During each of the quarters in the period from January 1, 2018 to 
December 31, 2018, the Service Company approved payments to third party vendors totaling $1, 970.7 million.   
The Summary of Selected Vendor Costs represents vendor costs “approved for payment” during each of the 
quarters in the period from January 1, 2018 to December 31, 2018, related to the selected vendors listed. 
 
This subject matter, designed to reflect a component of total vendor costs, was developed as follows.  The Finance 
Team obtained a list of amounts approved for payment by the Service Company (or the “Company”) to each 
vendor. For each quarter during the first half of the year, items were selected that represent the top 25 vendors 
based on dollars approved for payment in each quarter, 15 vendors selected without bias that are ranked between 
26 and 100 based on dollars approved for payment in each quarter, and 10 vendors selected without bias ranked 
greater than 100 based on dollars approved for payment in each quarter.  
 
For each quarter during the second half of the year, the Finance Team enhanced the testing procedures moving to 
a risk-based sampling and testing approach, in an effort to cover a larger number of unique transactions and greater 
number of vendors.  A unique transaction was defined as a vendor’s work for a particular project with a particular 
department at National Grid (i.e. If a vendor was performing work for one department under two projects, they 
would each be considered a unique transaction). The following methodology was followed: 
 
For these periods, the vendor population was stratified by certain significant transaction groups. When designing 
the testing approach for the individual transaction groups, consideration was given to the broader internal control 
environment.  To this effect, certain significant transaction groups were deemed to be tested 100% of the vendor 
population value, while others were sampled based on the risks identified, to achieve the test objectives. 
Specifically: 
 
 
Testing samples for the vendor population were selected to cover 40% every unique transaction, per vendor 
and a minimum of 10% of the invoices per unique transactions for Service Company vendors whose total 
Exhibit______(RRP-2)
Schedule 2
Page 77 of 100


--- Page 243 ---
 
expenditures were greater than $100 thousand dollars (96% of the population).  A unique transaction was 
defined as a vendor’s work for a particular project with a particular department at National Grid (e.g. If a 
vendor was performing work for one department under ten different projects, they would each be considered 
a unique transaction of which we would obtain 40 percent coverage [i.e. 4 projects].  A minimum of 10 
percent of the number of invoices associated with each of the unique transactions selected for testing would 
also examined). 
 
 
Service Company vendors which aggregated to less than $100 thousand dollars (~4% of the total population) 
would be subject to additional haphazard sampling. 
 
 
Basis of Accounting – Vendor costs included in the Summary of Selected Vendor Costs for each of the quarters in 
the period from January 1, 2018 to December 31, 2018 represent costs “approved for payment” for each named 
vendor during the period presented.  Irrespective of when the goods or services were received, for purposes of this 
presentation, vendor costs are considered approved for payment upon: 
 
- 
internal acknowledgment that the goods or services have been received, and 
- 
receipt of a vendor invoice. 
 
All costs included in the Summary of Selected Vendor Costs have been “approved for payment” by the Company, 
and properly allocated and charged to the Company and its affiliates, in accordance with the Company’s Cost 
Allocation Manual.  The Cost Allocation Manual is further described in Note 6. Note that vendor costs may have 
been incurred before the period from January 1, 2018 to December 31, 2018, but if both elements above were not 
present until after January 1, 2018 to December 31, 2018, such costs would consequently be “approved for 
payment” during the period presented and included in the accompanying Summary of Selected Vendor Costs.  
Likewise, vendor costs incurred during the period from January 1, 2018 to December 31, 2018, where 
bothelements above were not present prior to December 31, 2018, are not considered “approved for payment” 
during the period presented, nor included in the accompanying Summary of Selected Vendor Costs.  This 
accounting policy, applied in the Summary of Costs, is a basis of accounting other than GAAP and the FERC 
USoA. 
 
3. Labor Costs 
 
Summary of Selected Labor Costs – During the period from January 1, 2018 to December 31, 2018, the Company 
recorded costs to employees of $590.2 million in consideration for work undertaken for the benefit of the Company 
and its affiliates.  This amount includes base time and overtime pay but does not include labor-related overhead 
costs such as social security taxes, life insurance, pensions, post-retirement benefits other than pension, medical, 
dental and other welfare expenses. 
 
Given the large volume of transactions, items were selected that represented (i) the 15 largest cost centers and (ii) 
25 cost centers selected without bias ranked greater than 15, selected from a population consisting of the 15 largest 
operating departments as determined by payroll cost incurred, and 25 departments selected without bias ranked 
greater than 15, based on payroll cost incurred.  
 
Employees of the Company and its affiliates charge time to system work orders, similar to the process described 
above for vendor costs.  Labor costs are recorded by the Company’s payroll and time capture system.  Labor 
charges to work orders may be made by a direct employee of the Company, or by an employee of an affiliate 
company who is performing work for the benefit of the Company. 
 
Basis of accounting – Amounts presented in the Summary of Selected Labor Costs represent amounts due for 
base time and overtime to employees of the Company or its affiliates for time charged during the period presented 
Exhibit______(RRP-2)
Schedule 2
Page 78 of 100


--- Page 244 ---
 
and have been allocated consistent with the Company’s Cost Allocation Manual.  Amounts presented in the 
Summary of Selected Labor Costs have been charged to capital and operating cost line items within the general 
ledger in a manner consistent with nature of the work performed. 
 
 
 
4. Employee Expense Costs 
 
Summary of Selected Employee Expense Costs – During the period from January 1, 2018 to December 31, 2018, 
the Company approved payments to employees as reimbursement for business expenses incurred totaling $31.7 
million.  Business expenses are approved for payment if they are incurred in the normal course of business, in 
accordance with the Company’s internal policies, and include business travel, accommodation, spot purchases 
of goods, and other out-of-pocket expenses.  The Summary of Selected Employee Expense Costs includes a 
subset of such expenses.  This subject matter, designed to reflect a component of total employee expense costs, 
was developed as follows. The Finance Team obtained a list of amounts approved for payment by the Company 
in each quarter. Based upon this list, items were selected that represent the top 25 single employee claims (“trip 
reports”) and top 50 purchase credit card (“P-card”) transactions based on dollars approved for payment in each 
quarter, 15 trip reports selected without bias ranked between 26 and 100 based on dollars approved for payment 
in each quarter, 10 trip reports selected without bias ranked greater than 100 based on dollars approved for 
payment in each quarter, and 25 P-card transactions selected without bias ranked greater than 25 based on dollars 
approved for payment in each quarter. The Summary of Selected Employee Expense Costs also only includes 
expenses submitted by certain employees; it does not include any expenses submitted for reimbursement by 
“Band A” employees, defined as senior executives of NGUSA, as well as other costs which were excluded 
following a keyword search. 
 
Basis of accounting – Amounts presented in the Summary of Selected Employee Expense Costs represent 
employee expenses “approved for payment” during the period presented. Irrespective of when the expense was 
incurred, for purposes of this presentation, employee expenses are considered approved for payment upon 
submission by an employee of a request for reimbursement for a business expense, accompanied by evidence of 
the expense, and recoverable consistent with NGUSA’s US Business Travel & Expense Policy, effective January 
18, 2011, updated Feburary 16, 2017, with the exception of Section 17.1, which defines recoverable expenses 
that are subject to the P-card and other procurement guidelines (items recorded inconsistent with Section 19.1 
were still included in the Summary of Selected Employee Expense Costs if the business purpose for the expense 
was considered reasonable). This accounting policy, applied in the Summary of Costs, is a basis of accounting 
other than GAAP and the FERC USoA. 
 
All costs included in the accompanying Summary of Selected Employee Expense Costs have been allocated to the 
Companies in a manner consistent with the Company’s Cost Allocation Manual. 
 
5. General Ledger Entries 
 
Summary of Selected General Ledger Entries – During the period from January 1, 2018 to December 31, 2018, 
the Company recorded entries to the general ledger via automated journal entry and manual journal entry processes.  
Entries in the Company’s general ledger are assigned a “document type” (doc type), a unique two-digit code, 
designed to identify the source and nature of the journal entry.  The complete population of operating expenses 
recorded is an aggregation of amounts recorded under all doc types to the relevant general ledger accounts.  Costs 
approved for payment to vendors are recorded in the general ledger under doc types KR, RE, RS, and KG; labor 
costs are recorded under doc type AB; and employee expense costs under doc types TR and YU.  Entries recorded 
under the doc types KP, YV and WE are for the usage of materials, the inverse (receipt) of which is recorded 
initially as a RS or RE entry.

6.  Costs incurred and allocated by Service Company 
 
Cost Allocation Manual and Service Agreements 
Costs incurred by ServCo and by other NGUSA subsidiaries in providing services to NGUSA client 
companies (Client Companies), including the Company, are set forth in the service agreements and its Cost 
Allocation Manual (Revised April 2017) (CAM) and include, but are not limited to, labor and related overhead 
costs (e.g., salaries of officers and other employees, employee welfare expenses such as social security taxes, 
life insurance, pensions, post-retirement benefits other than pension, medical, dental and other welfare 
expenses), training costs, facilities costs, information technology costs, and costs related to vendor and other 
contract services.  The organization, conduct of business and method of cost allocation are designed to result 
Exhibit______(RRP-2)
Schedule 2
Page 81 of 100


--- Page 247 ---
 
in the performance of services and the provision of goods economically and efficiently for the benefit of the 
Client Companies at cost, fairly and equitably allocated among such companies. 
 
The purpose of the CAM is to serve as a guide as to the manner in which costs should be charged to the Client 
Companies by the company incurring the cost.  The prevailing premise of these cost allocation guidelines is 
that allocation methods should not result in subsidization of non-regulated services or products by regulated 
entities or subsidization of services or products from one regulated entity to another. 
 
The provision of administrative services to the Client Companies by ServCo is specified in service agreements 
filed with the respective utility regulatory commissions. 
 
Principles of cost allocation 
The following principles guide the allocation of costs of products or services provided by ServCo and 
other operating subsidiaries to the Client Companies. 
 
 Direct charging or direct assignment is the preferred allocation methodology and is used if the cost of 
providing a product or service can be identified with the Client Companies receiving the benefit of that 
product or service.  Direct charging should only be used if the cost of providing a product or service to an 
individual Client Company can be isolated and reported separately from costs to provide other products or 
services and from costs to provide the same product and service to other Client Companies. 
 
 The costs of products and services that cannot be direct charged should be allocated based on cost 
  causative allocation bases representative of the underlying cost drivers of that product or service. 
 
 The cost allocation methodology should be comprehensive, transparent, stable and administratively 
manageable and cost effective. 
 
 The calculation of the cost allocation bases should be supported by a clearly defined methodology, model 
and supporting policy and procedure documentation. 
 
 The cost allocation methodology should accommodate changes in the size of the allocation bases from 
period to period based on changes in the underlying cost drivers; the allocation bases should not vary 
significantly from period to period for uncontrollable factors not related to the underlying cost drivers. 
 
 
 The calculation of the allocation bases should be updated at least annually and more frequently if needed 
to reflect significant events (e.g., the sale of a significant affiliate). 
 
Costs are defined among the following four categories for purposes of allocating the costs of products and 
services to the Client Companies.  This hierarchy represents the order of methodologies used when allocating 
costs. These four cost categories are: 
 
 Directly Assignable – Expenses incurred for activities and services exclusively for the benefit of a Client 
Company. 
 
 Directly Attributable – Expenses incurred for activities and services that benefit more than one Client 
Company and which can be allocated based on direct measures of cost causation; for example, number of 
employees or number of customers. 
 
 Indirectly Attributable – Expenses incurred as a “cost of doing business” that do not relate to the provision 
of specific products and services. The costs typically benefit all entities within the corporate umbrella. 
Examples include governance costs, Corporate Secretary costs, and investor relations costs.  These costs 
Exhibit______(RRP-2)
Schedule 2
Page 82 of 100


--- Page 248 ---
 
are typically allocated based on a general measure of cost causation, commonly referred to as the general 
allocator. Costs that cannot be directly identified with the provision of a particular product or service.  
This includes but is not limited to governance costs, insurance, and taxes as well the cost of services 
supporting ServCo such as ServCo accounting and recruiting for ServCo positions. The general allocator 
is the ratio of net plant, net margins and net operations and maintenance expenses, equally weighted. 
 
 Unattributable – Expenses incurred for activities or services that have been determined as not 
appropriate for apportionment to the Client Companies.  These costs relate primarily to activities such as 
corporate diversification, political or philanthropic endeavors and, as such, are charged directly to the 
parent company, NGUSA. 
 
To apply these principles, ServCo and the Client Companies accumulate costs in system orders. The order 
design acts as the primary cost control element from which costs are billed to affiliates. For each order, an 
order design documents a description of the order’s use and purpose, the activities associated with that 
particular order, and justification for the allocation methodology to be used for allocating the costs 
accumulated in the order.  Only one allocation methodology can be used for each order. 
 
Subsidiaries charge no more than actual costs for services provided to the Company and other regulated 
affiliates.  
 
The monthly settlements process includes only the costs accumulated in the open orders.  There is no markup 
or profit included in allocations to the regulated affiliates.  The allocations are based on the methodologies 
designated and described above. Accordingly, the unit cost (price) charged to these affiliates, including the 
Company, is intended to reasonably approximate the actual costs of providing such services. 
 
Section 7 of the CAM lists those services provided by ServCo and the Client Companies to whom these services 
are provided. These services are provided in accordance with the service agreements filed with the respective 
utility regulatory commissions.

Supplementary information to the Summary of Costs- Service Company 
 
The total amounts recorded by the Company for the twelve-month period ended December 31, 2018 in general ledger accounts representing 
operating expenses are summarized in the table below.  The total ledger cost data (A) is the total of transactions recorded in the Company’s 
general ledger that relate to operating costs considered for recovery in customer rates. 
We have then subtracted items in the second column (B) costs incurred for energy efficiency programs and fleet, and accounting entries 
related to the accrual or deferral of regulatory accounting mechanisms, leaving the third column to show costs that the Finance Team selected 
and included in its examination (refer to the Notes to the Summary of Costs for more details on the method of selection).  Column C, and 
the immediately preceding columns (d-h), include amounts cross-referenced to the Summary of Costs.
